subject: SECURITY: rotate the neon CIFS share password - treat the current value as KNOWN
description:
The share credential was stored inline in /etc/fstab on bc1, which is mode 644 - every local account could read it (verified with sudo -u nobody test -r). Surfaced 2026-08-20 while diagnosing the power loss, and it was displayed during that troubleshooting session, so it must be treated as compromised.

DONE ALREADY (2026-08-20, commit 527e57dbe): moved to /etc/cifs-neon.creds mode 0600 root:root, created under umask 077 so there was never a world-readable window. fstab now uses credentials=. The two fstab backups also carried the inline password at 644 and were chmod 600 (kept, not deleted). Mount re-verified working after the change.

STILL TO DO - THIS IS THE ROTATION ITSELF, WHICH WAS NOT ATTEMPTED:
Moving a leaked secret to a better file does not un-leak it. The password must be changed on the Samba side on neon AND in /etc/cifs-neon.creds on every host that mounts the share, as one coordinated change - a half-rotated credential breaks the mount everywhere it is used, which is why it was deliberately left as an operator action rather than done mid-incident.

Steps: 1) find every host mounting //<neon>/shared (bc1 confirmed; check bc2/bc4/hexclass). 2) change the Samba password for that user on neon. 3) update /etc/cifs-neon.creds (0600) on each host. 4) remount and verify each. 5) confirm the probe's neon_share check returns up.

Addresses are in ~/hexworth-infra-private/ - this repo is public.
